title: How he got into the Missourians when Scotty went to jail
summary: Saxophonist Scotty gets six months under the Sullivan Law for carrying a gun, and the Missourians, prompted by Kansas City trumpeter Lamar Wright, call Thomas as a temporary replacement.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So then the guy... This is how I got in the Missourians. See, I often think back.... See, I just didn't realize in them days my worth. I was just a saxophone player trying to make it, man. And when Scotty got put in jail, they come lookin' for me...
What did he get put in jail for? Who was he playing with?

He was playing with the Missourians. And they put out the Sullivan Law. The Sullivan Law is, if you get caught with a gun, you just automatically got six months. There wasn't no bargaining; you got six months. So Scotty was involved with his wife or somebody in Harlem(?), and they caught him with a gun, and they put him in jail for six months.
So the guys... Now, see, I knew Lamar Wright from Topeka. Because he used to go with a girl, he used to date a girl at my school.
Now, Lamar Wright, the trumpet player, is from around Kansas City, wasn't he.
Yeah, he was from Kansas City.

And I knew him from Kansas City. Because he used to date Linda(?), a girl who was one of my classmates. So I just knew him well. I think it was him that influenced them to check me, to get me to play with the band. And I was only supposed to have the job six months. Because that's what Scotty got; he got six months.
Well, Lamar came to New York with the Missourians.
Yeah, he came in with them.
